summary: Enterprise AI model API aggregators are cloud-native platforms that provide secure, managed access to multiple foundation models (Claude, GPT, Llama, Gemini, Mistral, and more) through a unified API while keeping data within the customer's cloud boundary. As of 2026, there is no single winner — AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, and Google Vertex AI dominate by virtue of existing cloud contracts, while data-platform-native options like Snowflake Cortex and governance-focused platforms like IBM watsonx round out the landscape. The right choice is driven primarily by an enterprise's existing cloud footprint, required model breadth, and compliance posture rather than raw capability differences.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: inference runs inside the enterprise's own cloud tenant/VPC so proprietary data and prompts never leave the governed environment or get used for vendor model training
Compliance and governance: aggregators ship with SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, GDPR controls, audit logging, and access policies that are hard to replicate when calling vendor APIs directly
Single billing and procurement: consumption rolls into an existing cloud contract/committed spend (EDP, MACC), avoiding new vendor onboarding, separate invoices, and legal reviews
Model choice and avoidance of lock-in: one API provides access to many competing models (Claude, Llama, Mistral, Cohere, Gemini, GPT) so teams can swap models without re-architecting

Integration with existing cloud security and data stack: IAM, KMS encryption, private networking, and native connectors to data warehouses and storage reduce integration and security engineering effort

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service
available_models: Models via Azure AI Foundry (Llama, Mistral, Cohere, Phi)
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per 1K/1M tokens by model, plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity and predictable latency
key_features: VPC/private endpoints via Azure Private Link
Audit logs through Azure Monitor and Microsoft Purview
Fine-tuning support
Content filtering and responsible AI controls
Managed identity and RBAC via Entra ID
Data not used to train models
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first enterprises wanting OpenAI frontier models with deep M365, Azure, and Entra integration

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per token (on-demand), Batch discounts, and Provisioned Throughput for reserved capacity
key_features: VPC connectivity via AWS PrivateLink
Audit logging via CloudTrail and CloudWatch
Fine-tuning and custom model import
Knowledge Bases (RAG) and Agents
Guardrails for safety/PII filtering
KMS encryption; data not used to train base models
platforms.best_for: AWS-based enterprises wanting the widest model choice (especially Claude) behind one API

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per token/character/image, plus Provisioned Throughput sold in GSUs (e.g., 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash ≈ 67,250 tokens/sec sustained)
key_features: VPC Service Controls and Private Service Connect
Audit logs via Cloud Logging
Fine-tuning and distillation
Grounding with Google Search and enterprise data
MLOps via Vertex AI Pipelines
Data not used to train models
platforms.best_for: Data-heavy and ML-mature organizations on Google Cloud wanting Gemini plus a large Model Garden and strong MLOps

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based using Snowflake credits by model and function; billed within existing Snowflake contract
key_features: Inference runs inside the Snowflake data governance boundary
Cortex Analyst and Cortex Search (RAG)
Role-based access control inheriting Snowflake data policies
Audit via Snowflake access history
No data movement — LLMs come to the data
platforms.best_for: Enterprises whose governed data already lives in Snowflake and want LLMs applied without exporting data

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
available_models: Third-party and open-source Hugging Face models
platforms.pricing: Subscription plus consumption (Resource Units) per token; available on IBM Cloud, on-prem, and hybrid
key_features: Hybrid and on-premises deployment options
watsonx.governance for model risk, bias, and audit
Fine-tuning and prompt tuning (Tuning Studio)
Named Leader in 2026 Gartner MQ for DSML Platforms
watsonx Orchestrate for enterprise AI agents
IP indemnification on Granite models
platforms.best_for: Regulated enterprises needing strong AI governance, hybrid/on-prem control, and vendor indemnification

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per character/token and dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity
key_features: Dedicated AI clusters for isolated inference
VCN private networking
Audit logging via OCI Audit
Fine-tuning support
Tight integration with Oracle Fusion apps and Autonomous Database
platforms.best_for: Oracle-centric enterprises running Fusion Apps and Oracle databases wanting GenAI within OCI

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go priced in 'Neurons' (compute units) with a free tier; low-cost serverless edge inference
key_features: Globally distributed edge/serverless inference
AI Gateway for caching, rate limiting, and logging across providers
Vectorize vector database and R2 storage integration
Low-latency inference close to users
Observability and analytics per request
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises wanting cheap, low-latency serverless/edge inference and a unified gateway over multiple AI providers

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based (DBUs) for model serving and training within existing cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) contracts
key_features: Unity Catalog governance and lineage for data and models
Model Serving with private networking
Fine-tuning and custom model training on governed data
Vector Search and RAG tooling
MLflow for lifecycle management and audit
platforms.best_for: Lakehouse-centric enterprises wanting to build, fine-tune, and serve models directly on governed data with strong MLOps
